newsitem.title: USA: Former H&R Block employee convicted.
newsitem.headline: Former H&R Block employee convicted.

text.p: A former employee of the H&R Block company has been convicted of 17 felony tax charges for preparing false federal income tax returns for clients, federal prosecutors said Thursday.
Sandy Amoyaw, 42, faces a possible maximum sentence of years in prison and $250,000 fines on each of the 17 counts. He was convicted by a Manhattan federal jury late Wednesday.

Amoyaw was charged with preparing false income tax returns on behalf of 16 clients. The returns, which were filed for the 1989 calendar year, contained fictitious and inflated deductions for medical expenses, charitable contributions, job expenses and child care.
The defendant was working at H&R Block at the time but also had his own tax preparation business. Most of the false returns were filed for his own personal clients.
The evidence at trial showed that more than 90 other returns that Amoyaw prepared contained similar deductions.
Amoyaw was also convicted of filing his own false income tax return.
